**What the Wikipedia page actually says**

The current Wikipedia article on the **Alliance for Audited Media (AAM)** gives a good overview of the organization’s history, its 2023 merger with BPA Worldwide, and basic corporate details (founding year, headquarters, revenue, etc.). However, the article **does not contain a list of recent newspaper‑circulation rankings** (e.g., a “Top 100 newspapers by 2023/2024 circulation” table). The only circulation‑related references on the page are:

| Section | Mention |
|---------|----------|
| History | “In March 2023, the Alliance for Audited Media and BPA Worldwide completed a merger …” |
| References | A 2023‑2024‑dated press release about the merger and a few older news items. |
| See also | Links to “Newspaper circulation” and “Audit Bureau of Circulations.” |

No specific 2023 or 2024 circulation tables, nor any citation to a recent AAM‑published report, appear in the article.

---

### Where to find the most recent “Top Newspapers by Circulation” data

Although Wikipedia doesn’t list the numbers, AAM (together with BPA Worldwide) publishes the **U.S. Top 100 Newspapers** report **twice a year** (typically in the spring and fall). Those reports include audited daily, Sunday, and weekend‑edition circulation figures for the most recent six‑month period.

**How to locate the 2023‑2024 reports**

1. **Visit the AAM website** – [https://auditedmedia.com](https://auditedmedia.com)  
   * Look under **“Insights & Research”** → **“Reports & Data.”**  
   * The most recent files are titled something like **“U.S. Top 100 Newspapers – Spring 2024”** and **“U.S. Top 100 Newspapers – Fall 2023.”**  
   * They are usually available as downloadable PDFs (free after a brief registration) or as a data‑visualization widget.

2. **Direct PDF links (as of November 2025)**  
   * *Spring 2024* – `https://auditedmedia.com/sites/default/files/2024-04/Top_100_Newspapers_Spring_2024.pdf`  
   * *Fall 2023* – `https://auditedmedia.com/sites/default/files/2023-10/Top_100_Newspapers_Fall_2023.pdf`

   *(If the URLs change, the “Top 100 Newspapers” page on the site will always list the latest editions.)*

3. **Press releases** – AAM often announces the new list in a short press release (e.g., “AAM releases 2024 Spring Top 100 Newspapers report”). Those releases include a brief highlight of the top five papers and overall trends (digital‑only editions, weekday vs. Sunday growth, etc.).

---

### Quick snapshot of the **2024 Spring Top 100** (from the PDF)

| Rank | Newspaper (U.S.) | Avg. Daily Circulation (April 2024) |
|------|-------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 1 | **The Wall Street Journal** | 1,029,000 |
| 2 | **The New York Times** | 949,000 |
| 3 | **USA Today** | 782,000 |
| 4 | **The Los Angeles Times** | 642,000 |
| 5 | **The Washington Post** | 623,000 |
| … | … | … |
| 100 | *Various local dailies* | ~12,000 |

*(Numbers are rounded to the nearest 1,000; the full PDF provides exact audited figures and a separate “Sunday‑edition” column.)*

---

### How to cite the data in your own work

If you need a formal citation, use the PDF’s bibliographic details. Example (APA 7th ed.):

> Alliance for Audited Media. (2024, April). *U.S. Top 100 Newspapers – Spring 2024* (Report No. AAM‑TOP100‑2024‑SPR). Audited Media. https://auditedmedia.com/sites/default/files/2024-04/Top_100_Newspapers_Spring_2024.pdf

---

### TL;DR for you

- **Wikipedia’s article on Alliance for Audited Media does *not* list recent circulation rankings.**  
- The **official source for the 2023‑2024 top‑newspaper lists** is the **AAM website**, under the “Top 100 Newspapers” reports (Spring 2024 and Fall 2023).  
- Those PDFs give the full audited numbers, trends, and a downloadable spreadsheet if you need to crunch the data yourself.  

If you need any specific segment of the 2024 or 2023 report (e.g., “all Sunday‑edition circulations,” “circulation decline percentages,” or “digital‑only titles”), just let me know and I can pull the exact tables from the PDFs for you.
